"Whilst we foresee the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield finding its way higher towards 4.5% from a structural perspective, we do think the shutdown will prevent that move from materialising for now," ING rates strategists wrote in a note.

content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Rise, Led by Long-Dated Yields
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were rising, particularly long-dated yields, as the U.S. government shutdown drags on into a second week.  This means official U.S. data, including key monthly nonfarm payrolls numbers due last week, won't be released.  Focus this week will be on Wednesday's Federal Reserve minutes for clues on how fast interest rates are likely to fall.
